positive: Definitional verbs and phrases: 'means', 'meaning', 'refers to', 'is defined as', 'defined', '是指', '指的是', '意为', 'i.e.' (即); also code 'def' tokens. Fires on the defining verb in 'X means/refers to ...' sentences, e.g. in glossary-style educational text.
negative: '-man'/'man' suffix tokens, 'Based', 'Using'/'using', 'ITS'; fires weakly negative on 'Based on ...' and 'Using ...' sentence openers.

positive: Multiple-choice answer contexts: option letters '(C', '(B', '[C', the answer phrase '故选' ('so choose') or '下列' ('which of the following'), 'ANS'; also 'Points'/'points' in scoring text.
negative: Uppercase two-letter tokens and abbreviations ('OK', 'DP', 'AG', 'AS', 'AX', 'AF'), arrows and comparisons ('==>', '-->', '<='), and closing words ('concluding', 'ending', 'Central').

positive: Chemistry and materials-science terms: spectroscopy ('spectro', 'спект'), electrolysis, magnesium (Mg), alloys, crystals (晶体), melting, hydrates; also 'Christmas' and day names such as 'Tuesday'.
negative: Physics and solid-state terms: 'vacuum', 'filament', 'vibrating', 'inert', 'carbon', 'solid' (固态), 'irradiated', 'excess', 'energetic'; also 'successive' and 'characteristic'.

positive: Sentence-ending punctuation, especially after a closing bracket or quote: ').', '].', '").', '.).', '°.', and the full-width stop '。' or Urdu/Hindi '۔'/'।'; also some clause-final ';' after a quote, and 'etc'.
negative: Common mid-sentence verbs and adjectives: 'makes', 'make', 'gives', 'will', 'fair', 'familiar', 'closely', 'paired', 'folded'; also a lone ',' after a space.

positive: Weak and diffuse; possibly money and price words ('expensive', '美元' ('US dollar'), 'dollars') and words for places or continents.
negative: Strongly negative on the concept 'destroy' in any language: 'destroy', 'destroyed', 'destruction', 'destruct', 'zerstören', 'разру-', 'уничто-', '摧毁', '破坏', '毁灭', 'destruir', and code 'Destroy'/'.destroy'.

positive: 'families' and 'family' tokens in several languages ('familias', 'famílias', '-family'), 'casas' ('houses'), '_values', 'Rs' (rupees); lexical, layer 1.
Prose transition and discourse words in non-code text: '然而' ('however'), 'accordingly', 'Rest'; also '---@' annotations and CSS-like '.background'/'.align'; diffuse.
negative: Strongly negative on tab-indented code: a token that starts with a tab ('\tif', '\tfor', '\tS', '\tC', ...), i.e. the first token of an indented line in source code.

positive: Video-game and fantasy mechanics: 'summon', 'game', 'RAW', 'RUN', 'stack', 'tree' (树林 ('woods')), 'Accum'; also historical names such as '刘备' (Liu Bei). The output pushes toward 'final', 'plate', 'solid' and away from 'mode'.
negative: Chinese words for institutions and collectives: '机关' ('government agency'), '文明' ('civilization'), '选拔' ('selection'), '团' ('group'), '分布' ('distribution'); also 'Selector', 'Clan', 'simulate', 'DLC', '-themed'.

positive: Weak and diffuse: tokens meaning 'set/establish' ('定' ('fix'), 'establishing', '打下' ('lay a foundation')), 'handling'/'处理' ('handle'), 'core'. Output promotes 'set' and '成功' ('success').
negative: Strongly negative on restrictive 'only' words in many languages: 'only', 'solely', 'только', 'tylko', 'nur', 'apenas', 'únicamente', 'uniquement', 'sadece', '只有' ('only'), '仅限' ('limited to'), '局限于' ('confined to'); also 'focused'/'-focused' (as in 'focused on').

positive: Openings of LaTeX math: '$', '$\\', '\\ln', '\\tan', 'modular'; also short function words such as 'al', 'por', 'ie', 'alt'. Output promotes '\\frac' and 'fraction'. Likely fires in math solutions just before a formula.
negative: Strongly negative on fraction words: 'half', 'halves', 'third(s)', 'quarter', 'fraction(s)', '三分之一' ('one-third'), '四分之一' ('one-quarter'), '一半' ('half'), 'Drittel', 'setengah', 'половину'. Example: math word problems such as 'half of the apples' or 'one-third of the students'.
